name: Cruising on TRT

card.summary: Staying on a replacement-range testosterone regimen between higher-intake periods instead of stopping, so practitioners keep the muscle, fullness and energy they built.
card.note: Involves prescription hormones; medical monitoring of blood counts, prostate markers and fertility is standard in clinical TRT.

quick.overview:
Cruising is the term used in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing circles for continuing a testosterone regimen at replacement-range levels between periods of higher hormone intake (often called blasting). People who do it say it preserves the muscle mass, leanness and general fuller look they gained, rather than losing it after stopping.

Clinically, testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is a prescribed treatment for hypogonadism with its own monitoring requirements. Forum discussion of cruising draws on physiology papers on androgen receptors and on personal experience; no clinical trials have tested the blast-and-cruise pattern.
quick.how: Practitioners describe alternating between higher-intake phases and a steady lower phase, rather than coming fully off. Discussions focus on timing, bloodwork and how the body feels, and some link the pattern to androgen receptor adaptation.
quick.risks: TRT can raise red blood cell counts, suppress sperm production and affect sleep apnea, and monitoring of PSA and hematocrit is recommended in clinical care. Stopping or changing hormone regimens can also bring mood and energy changes that some forum posters describe as difficult.

lead: Cruising on TRT refers to staying on a testosterone replacement-range regimen between higher-intake periods instead of stopping completely. The term comes from bodybuilding culture, where higher-intake phases are called blasts, and the lower steady phase is the cruise. Practitioners describe the goal as holding on to muscle, fullness and energy while avoiding the drop that can follow a full stop.

Clinically, testosterone replacement therapy supplements androgens and is prescribed mainly for male hypogonadism. It can be given by injection, gel, patch, cream, tablet or pellet, and it has anabolic effects on muscle mass and bone density [2]. The cruising pattern itself, as used in lifting communities, is not a clinical protocol.

On looksmax.org, users discuss why blasting and cruising might work, citing a study in which skeletal muscle androgen receptor expression more than doubled at one month of testosterone administration and was back to baseline by six months [1]. Other posts describe the cruise phase as hard, with one user reporting weakness and distress during it [3].

chain: Stay on a replacement-range regimen between higher-intake phases
Hormone levels do not drop to baseline
Muscle, leanness and energy are retained for continued training
angle.text: Practitioners say cruising keeps their physique closer to its peak between pushes. This is a community-reported rationale; the pattern has not been tested in clinical trials.

paras: In lifting culture the cruise is a lower, steady-hormone period that follows or precedes higher-intake phases. The idea is to avoid stopping entirely, which people describe as followed by a loss of muscle and a rough recovery.

A forum post titled around androgen receptor down-regulation argues that continuous high intake blunts receptor expression and that alternating high and cruise phases lets the body respond again, citing a study showing receptor expression returning to baseline over six months of continuous testosterone [1].
Other users describe the cruise as physically and emotionally difficult, noting lost strength and appetite for gains despite eating heavily [3].

TRT is the standard treatment for hypogonadism and shows anabolic effects on muscle and bone [2]. Reported adverse effects include increased hematocrit, suppressed sperm production, worsened sleep apnea and possible blood clots, and clinicians recommend a baseline digital rectal exam and PSA test followed by monitoring [2].
In 2025 the FDA removed a boxed cardiovascular warning for testosterone products, citing the TRAVERSE trial, though long-term safety is not fully known [2].
No studies found on cruising as a protocol. Clinical research on TRT in hypogonadal men is summarised on the testosterone replacement therapy page [2].

lore.intro: Cruising is discussed as the counterpart to blasting in androgen-use threads [1][3].

claims.claim: Alternating blast and cruise phases lets androgen receptors recover.
claims.believers: Posters cite a study where muscle androgen receptor expression rose at one month and returned to baseline by six months of continuous testosterone [1].
claims.experts: No published trials have tested blast-and-cruise cycling against continuous regimens.

claims.claim: Staying on replacement range preserves gains.
claims.believers: Practitioners say they hold more muscle on a cruise than after fully stopping [3].
claims.experts: Clinical TRT research reports anabolic effects on muscle in hypogonadal men, but not in this usage pattern [2].
